lede: A regular season good enough to win most years: 14–5, 4.9 categories a week, fourth seed. Then a 2–7 quarter-final loss to Brighton, a 9–0 win over the Foxes, and a sixth-place finish after a final week in which only 38 starting slots were set. Ats won the regular season two ways: a draft that supplied 62% of the team's category value, and the third-best wire record in the league.
profile: Blocks were the anchor: won in 20 of 22 matchups, second in the league with 570. Around them, a team that was quietly fourth in five categories — points, threes, rebounds, steals and turnovers. That is rare breadth. The one real hole is assists: 12th of 14, 5–16–1. It is a punt nobody chose — the drafted core is bigs and wings, with no lead ball-handler. FG% at 10th, despite the bigs, is the wings' volume shooting.
ledger: 108 of 198 categories. The one-category weeks went 5–1 — close games were won. Brighton is the story. The Infirmary played them three times and lost all three — 4–5 in week 10, 3–6 in week 18, 2–7 in the playoffs. A blocks-and-counting team has little to fall back on against another team of bigs that wins FG% every week. That matchup, not the 14–5 record, decided the season.
draft: The middle of the board carried it. Trey Murphy III at $24 was the best pick for the price on the roster: 0.76 categories a week, +0.35 over par. Chet Holmgren at $38 (+0.16) and Bam Adebayo at $28 (+0.15) both beat what their prices usually buy, and the $9 wings did too: Jaden McDaniels +0.31, Toumani Camara +0.18. The misses were cheap and quick. Bennedict Mathurin ($8, −0.25), Zaccharie Risacher ($5, −0.21) and Christian Braun ($9, a good call on the board that delivered −0.20) were all gone early. Zach LaVine and Norman Powell left in the day-34 trade, whose return the data cannot see.
production: 38% of the value came from players acquired after the draft, below most of the league. The biggest addition was the best player on the roster by rate: Anthony Edwards, +0.81 a week, started in all 14 weeks he was held. Kevin Porter Jr. added +0.52 a week. P.J. Washington, claimed on day 25, added a modest +0.29 in the regular season and then +1.36 over three playoff weeks.
trades: Only two trades all season. Day 34 sent LaVine and Powell to Ben's Need Some VC. The incoming side leaves no trace in the data, so it is not graded, though Edwards joined the lineup the next day. Day 49, Franz Wagner for Kyshawn George, grades "lucky break on a poor call". On what was knowable, Wagner's line was worth more (−0.20 expected). But Wagner started two of his next ten weeks for Brighton, and George delivered +0.30 a week over 12 weeks. Either it was selling at exactly the right moment or selling a player the numbers could not yet see was hurt. The record cannot say which.
wire: +0.10 categories a week per move against the player replaced, third in the league, from 67 claims won out of 330 attempts, all $100 of FAAB spent and never more than $10 on one player. The best moves came late: Sam Hauser for Jalen Pickett on day 91 ("good call, and it paid off", +0.46 a week) and Derrick Jones Jr. for Trae Young on day 128 (+0.41). The costliest lasting ones were poor calls at the time too: Jalen Green for Sandro Mamukelashvili on day 73 (−0.19 over nine weeks) and Keegan Murray for Peyton Watson on day 29 (−0.16 over 14).
bench: Twenty wasted player-days, 560 production — second most in the league. Three of the six biggest came on the final day of the season: Gary Trent Jr. 48, Toumani Camara 37 and Devin Carter 35, all benched on day 160. Across the regular season the lineup was well managed.
last: The fifth-place game, and it looks like the season had already ended for this roster. 38 starting slots set against 50, and one of nine on the final day. The result was 3–6, with points 507 to 810 and assists 87 to 190. It cost a place in the final standings and nothing more. But it is on the page.
closing: A strong manager's season. The draft found value from $9 to $28, the wire was among the league's best, and the one trade that can be graded came out +0.30 a week. A 14–5 record is not an accident. It ended against the one opponent built to beat it. The fix is in the category profile: assists at 5–16–1 is a free category handed to every opponent, every week. One genuine playmaker would have made the Brighton matchup — and every close week — a different calculation. Keep the wire approach exactly as it is. It was the best thing about this team.
